diagnostic_evidence.quote: so we may take $C_t:=1$ to prove Remark \ref{rmk:p}

issues.failure_explanation: The inequality ||f||_p <= ||f||_inf only shows that an L^p-approximate design is a sup-approximate design. The remark asserts the converse, which would need ||f||_inf <= C_t||f||_p; by Nikolskii-type bounds C_t grows polynomially in t. Hence an error bound eps||f||_inf does not give eps||f||_p.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: are pairwise disjoint for all $y\in Y\setminus\{y_0\}$, as for any $y\in Y$ and $j\in\{1,...,n_y\}$, we have

issues.failure_explanation: For j=n_y the outgoing point is g_{z_y}(1)e^{i delta}, and delta may be 0. It can then coincide with the endpoint g_{z_y}(1) of the incoming edge, so the arcs in D_y and D_{d_{y,n_y}} overlap; for n_y=1 this is forced whenever delta<delta-tilde. The argument checks only consecutive outgoing arcs, not the incoming one. The length identity |union D_y| = delta and the surgery to a single circle then fail.

issues.failure_explanation: D_t is the maximal nearest-neighbour distance, not the covering radius, and the two-sided claim is false for arbitrary design sequences: Y_t cup U Y_t, with U unitary near the identity, is still a design but has arbitrarily small D_t. The main proof needs an upper bound on the covering radius, which an upper bound on D_t does not give, since clustered sets have long MST edges. The mechanism is 'other' because this is a cited statement with no in-source argument to fault.
